package_info.package_versions: latest version prior to removal (exact version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The CamScanner app included a hidden Trojan Dropper module within a third-party advertising library, which enabled the download and installation of additional malicious programs on user devices without consent. This behavior constitutes a severe violation of user trust and platform policy, making the entire package malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon app launch or ad library invocation)
execution_context.file_location: third-party advertising library embedded in the CamScanner APK

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code contacts a remote command-and-control server to retrieve a URL, downloads a malicious payload (APK), saves it to the device's storage, and attempts to install it, resulting in the device being infected with additional malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and installs executable code from an external server at runtime, a classic behavior of Trojan Dropper malware. This enables arbitrary code execution and further compromise of the device.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate PDF creator app should not download or install additional APKs or executable code from the internet after installation. Such behavior is not required for the app's advertised functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate apps may update themselves or download plugins, but this is typically done through official app store mechanisms and with explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Hidden code in third-party ad library
Runtime download and installation of APKs
No user interaction required for payload installation

attack_chain.action: User installs CamScanner from the Google Play Store, unknowingly receiving the malicious ad library.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present on the device, awaiting execution.

attack_chain.action: Upon app launch or ad library invocation, the Trojan Dropper code executes and contacts a remote C2 server.
The dropper downloads a malicious APK and installs it on the device, enabling further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device is infected with additional malware, which may steal data or perform other malicious actions.

behavioral_signatures: Android app downloading and installing APKs from non-official sources at runtime
Hidden code in third-party ad libraries performing network requests to unknown domains
Unprompted installation of additional packages after initial app installation
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious APK files in app data directories (e.g., /data/data/com.camscanner/payload.apk)
Obfuscated or encrypted code within embedded ad libraries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains or IPs associated with malware distribution
Dynamic retrieval of payload URLs from remote servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android apps for runtime behaviors involving the download and installation of APKs from external sources, especially when initiated by embedded third-party libraries. Analyze network traffic for connections to suspicious domains and inspect app packages for obfuscated code or hidden modules capable of executing such actions. Flag apps that attempt to install additional packages without explicit user consent or outside of official update mechanisms.
